dataset.attribution: AIT Data Compression Challenge 2026 (AITDCC 2026), Ribeiro et al.

lzbench.scope: Standalone per-file codecs, using the original bytes. These are independent tests, not competition scores.

unsupported_codec_probe.note: The distribution printed NOT FOUND per file despite returning zero. Those lines have no CSV sizes and were excluded.

flitzfs_collective.mode: Native indexed and mirrored, ingest Zstandard level 3, CPU collective controller with modeled idle opportunities
flitzfs_collective.image_workload_scope: Ordinary indexed writes, pre- and post-maintenance compacted copies, independent CPU byte verification. Selector accounted separately.

cpython_revisions.selection: First twelve changed paths in ordinal name order in Python, Objects, Modules or Lib, with both versions sized 64–192 KiB inclusive and extensions .c .h .py .txt. File order is by version then path. All bytes are unmodified.

historical_control.corpus: Silesia tar used by lzbench upstream
historical_control.scope: The one-block probe cleared Zstandard and Brotli rows. The LZMA row returned a compression error. No aggregate claim was made.

asan_configuration_retry.cause: The first build selected the default configuration. A stale RelWithDebInfo executable rejected the new option; the exact configuration was rebuilt before qualification.

limits: This pilot measures local engine and standalone codec behavior on the actual Windows host. It supplies no mounted NTFS, mounted FlitzFS, or physical device rates.
The AIT driver measures collective grouping and includes no persistent coherence store or automatic cold-codec rewrite.

The AMD revision fixture offers the existing route explicitly, uses modeled idle opportunities, and binds the same source data and physical AMD worker in each paired trial. It does not establish that automatic policy should choose this route.
